articles.title: Caesars gives NFL legend a ‘looksmaxxing’ makeover in sportsbook ads
articles.summary: Caesars Sportsbook debuted "We've Had Some Work Done," a national campaign launched Wednesday to coincide with the NFL season opener and Clay Matthews' Sept. 10 debut as a Netflix sportscaster. The 15- and 30-second spots feature Matthews sporting an exaggerated "looksmaxxing" transformation, complete with an oversized jawline and inflated calf muscles, achieved through practical prosthetics and makeup from Legacy Effects rather than AI or digital filters. The makeover serves as a metaphor for the sportsbook's own overhaul since its 2021 launch, highlighting a redesigned app, new rewards system and features like Flex Parlays. Created with minority-owned agency Fellow Kids and produced by Hungry Man under director Dave Laden, the campaign was teased by TMZ beforehand to generate viral buzz, echoing tactics used in CeraVe's Michael Cera push. Caesars SVP Samira Zebian said the goal was making the app's evolution "impossible to miss" as the brand competes against DraftKings and FanDuel in the crowded sports betting market. The campaign will run across TV, digital and social channels throughout the football season.
articles.li_summary: Caesars Sportsbook launched "We've Had Some Work Done," a new ad campaign featuring ex-NFL star Clay Matthews with an exaggerated "looksmaxxing" makeover, promoting app redesigns and features like Flex Parlays ahead of the NFL season.

articles.title: X adds new anti-lawsuit provision to terms of service
articles.summary: X revised its Terms of Service on Wednesday, requiring all users to accept the new terms to keep using the platform. Legal disputes will now be handled specifically in Texas courts under Texas law, reflecting X's ties to SpaceX, which is headquartered there. The update also sharpens user-responsibility language, stating users are accountable for actions taken through features that act autonomously on their behalf, echoing Elon Musk's past comments about personal liability for illegal content generated via xAI tools. Most notably, X added explicit language stating users waive their right to a jury trial and to join or bring class, collective, or representative actions, extending this to corporate affiliates where legally allowed. This comes as X faces a class action from sexual abuse survivors alleging xAI's Grok chatbot generated and distributed child sexual abuse material, with one plaintiff claiming Grok was trained using existing CSAM tied to them. Similar waivers already exist at Twitter, Meta, and TikTok, and haven't historically stopped class actions, so enforceability of X's updated clause remains uncertain.
articles.li_summary: X updated its Terms of Service on Wednesday, adding explicit jury-trial and class-action waivers for all users, requiring Texas courts under Texas law, amid an active lawsuit alleging Grok generated CSAM.

articles.title: Meta keeps trying to make digital assistants happen
articles.summary: Meta released Muse, a new AI-powered chatbot app that lets users name their assistant, converse with it, and assign tasks it can complete autonomously in the background, positioning it as Mark Zuckerberg's latest step toward "personal superintelligence for everyone." This mirrors Meta's 2015 "M" assistant, which former Messenger chief David Marcus said could book restaurants, arrange travel, and purchase gifts, but which was discontinued in January 2018 after failing to attract sustained user interest. Meta also previously tried celebrity-themed chatbots and Messenger bots in 2016, none of which gained traction despite heavy promotion. Zuckerberg described his own use of Muse as wanting help to "be a better father and a better husband" and show up more for friends, revealing an optimization-driven mindset toward maximizing efficiency in daily life. Critics argue this reflects a mismatch with most users, who value human interaction and everyday tasks like shopping or research as meaningful experiences rather than inefficiencies to eliminate, suggesting Muse may repeat the same underwhelming reception as Meta's earlier assistant products.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched its Muse AI assistant app this week, letting users name and delegate background tasks to a chatbot, echoing its failed 2015 "M" personal assistant that was shelved in January 2018 due to low adoption.

articles.title: Pinterest shares insights into men’s trends
articles.summary: Pinterest released a trend breakdown covering men's search behavior heading into 2026, aimed at helping marketers refine targeting as men now represent roughly a third of the platform's 640 million monthly active users. The report groups rising interests into themes: wellness and travel resets like "wellness retreats" (+83%) and "road trip ideas" (+126%); active social outings such as "Hyrox" (+193%) and "padel event" (+47%); hands-on hobbies including "easy woodworking projects" (+316%) and "junk journaling ideas" (+214%); home entertaining touches like "charcuterie board design" (+390%) and "record player setup" (+223%); grooming and beauty shifts such as "Italian beard fade" (+725%) and "modern wolf cut men" (+553%); nail color trends including "silver nails men" (+87%); skincare growth with overall men's product searches up 280% and "red light mask" (+156%); fragrance interest via "perfume discovery set" (+167%); and fashion movements spanning workwear-inspired looks, leather goods like "handmade leather wallet" (+290%), and pink clothing items such as "dusty pink shirt outfit men" (+283%). Pinterest frames these shifts as a roadmap for brands building Pin ad campaigns targeting male users.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest published its 2026 men's trend report, highlighting search spikes like "Italian beard fade" (+725%), "modern wolf cut men" (+553%) and "charcuterie board design" (+390%), as men now make up a third of its 640 million monthly users.

articles.title: Snap CEO discusses ad development and AI
articles.summary: In a letter marking Snap's 15th anniversary, CEO Evan Spiegel laid out the company's advertising roadmap, centered on what he calls "generative advertising." Rather than relying on explicit intent signals like search queries or cart additions, Spiegel wants AI-driven multimodal models to analyze user behavior and friend connections to predict what people might want next, then match them with relevant businesses, potentially generating new demand instead of just capturing existing intent. He also highlighted creator partnerships as a growing ad opportunity, noting creator-made ads are watched 25% longer and generate 16% more active attention than standard branding ads, with over 300,000 creators now eligible for brand collaborations. Spiegel additionally plans to make product discovery and sharing easier within the app, organically surfacing shopping-related content to drive purchases. Beyond advertising, Spiegel criticized unnamed "ruthless competitors" for copying Snapchat's features and pushed back against grouping Snapchat with broader "social media," citing studies linking Snapchat use to improved friendship closeness, peer support, and overall wellbeing, though he acknowledged these findings show correlation rather than proven causation.
articles.li_summary: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel used a 15th-anniversary staff letter to unveil plans for "generative advertising," using AI to predict user desires and recommend products before they search, while touting creator ads' 25% longer play time and 16% higher attention versus standard brand ads.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse personal AI
articles.summary: Meta has released Muse, a new AI agent app and in-stream chatbot integrated with users' Facebook and Instagram profiles, letting people name their own assistant and delegate tasks such as trip planning, ticket booking, email sending, and form completion. Muse can also complete purchases directly within conversations, raising data-privacy concerns
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent app that plans tasks, books travel, fills out forms, and completes in-stream purchases, running on a dedicated "Muse Secure VM" co-designed with Signal's Moxie Marlinspike, with 100 million free weekly tokens per user.

articles.title: Campbell’s heats up digital focus amid marketing reformulation
articles.summary: Campbell's Company is overhauling its marketing strategy after total net sales fell 8% year over year in fiscal Q4 2026 and 5% for the full year, with snacks organic sales down 6%. CEO Mick Beekhuizen said about 85% of the working media budget will now go toward social media, influencers, e-commerce and AI-powered platforms, shifting from an evenly-spread portfolio approach to concentrating fiscal 2027 spend on top growth brands: Rao's, Goldfish, Pepperidge Farm and Campbell's itself. Rao's, acquired via Sovos Brands three years ago, saw consumption grow 9.4% and household penetration near 19%, prompting another round of double-digit media spending increases and a new campaign about slow-simmered sauces and shared meals. Goldfish, seen as critical to snacks' turnaround, is getting a back-to-school omnichannel campaign from Mischief @ No Fixed Address emphasizing real cheese and no artificial ingredients, plus new protein, whole-grain and gluten-free varieties this fall. The marketing overhaul is partly funded by a $500 million cost-savings plan that includes a 13% salaried workforce reduction and closure of two snack plants.
articles.li_summary: Campbell's will direct roughly 85% of its working media budget to social media, influencers, e-commerce and AI-driven platforms in fiscal 2027, concentrating spend on Rao's, Goldfish, Pepperidge Farm and the Campbell's brand while cutting 13% of salaried staff.

articles.title: Pinterest renames campaign objectives to simplify ad focus
articles.summary: Pinterest is overhauling the naming of campaign objectives within its Ads Manager platform to help advertisers more easily match campaign types to business goals. The previous "Conversions" and "Catalog Sales" objectives are being renamed to "Leads," "Sales," and "Consideration" depending on context, with Pinterest clarifying that Leads campaigns target non-transactional actions like signups, while Sales campaigns focus on transactional actions such as add-to-carts and checkouts. Pinterest also released an updated objective guide to help advertisers choose the right campaign type for their goals. The company confirmed this is purely a naming and clarity update, not a functional change, meaning advertisers won't see any shifts in campaign performance or ramp times, which will still depend on creative sources as before. Existing campaigns built under the old Conversions and Catalog Sales labels will remain editable until April 30, 2027, after which they'll be archived. While a minor structural tweak, the change is meant to reduce confusion for both current advertisers and newcomers setting up Pin campaigns on the platform.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest is renaming Ads Manager objectives, replacing "Conversions" and "Catalog Sales" with "Leads," "Sales," and "Consideration" to clarify campaign goals, with old campaigns editable until April 30, 2027 before archiving.

articles.title: Will removing algorithmic sorting improve social media?
articles.summary: Australia's government is pushing forward a policy that would force social media platforms to make algorithmic feed sorting an opt-in feature rather than the default, giving users the choice to view chronological content instead. The move responds to growing evidence that algorithmic amplification promotes divisive, rage-inducing content and worsens political polarization. However, platforms including Meta have long argued that engagement drops sharply without algorithms—Facebook noted back in 2014 that with algorithmic ranking, users read 70% of available stories versus just 57% without it, since the average user faced roughly 1,500 potential feed stories per visit. Meta's repeated internal testing since then has consistently shown chronological feeds reduce reading, likes, and comments compared to algorithmic sorting. The article argues that while removing algorithms might hurt platform engagement metrics, it could benefit users by reducing time spent scrolling and exposure to divisive content, though it may also increase content overwhelm and echo chambers. With user behavior toward curating feeds having evolved significantly since 2014, Australia's smaller market could serve as a useful real-world testing ground for measuring the actual impact of removing algorithmic defaults.
articles.li_summary: Australia is advancing legislation requiring social platforms to make algorithmic content sorting opt-in, letting users switch to chronological feeds despite Meta's data showing engagement drops significantly without algorithmic ranking.

articles.title: Australia moves to enable algorithm opt-outs
articles.summary: Australia's government announced Tuesday it will pursue legislation requiring social media platforms to notify both new and existing users, giving them an explicit choice between an algorithm-driven default feed or a chronological one showing only content from accounts they follow. Currently most platforms bury opt-out settings in menus, and only X and Threads offer a "Following" feed as a selectable default, and only on desktop. This policy would make Australia the largest real-world test of algorithm-free social media, potentially revealing how much engagement-based recommendation systems contribute to misinformation spread and divisive content amplification. Beyond feed defaults, the government also plans new rules targeting addictive app features and AI chatbots, plus stricter controls on content involving eating disorders, crime, gender equality issues, and dangerous stunts. Regulators would be authorized to fine noncompliant platforms up to $109.2 million, with detailed rules to be finalized in coming months. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's office framed the move as boosting protection from harmful content while expanding user choice. The change could influence global policy debates and force publishers to rethink audience-engagement strategies if algorithmic feeds lose their default dominance.
articles.li_summary: Australia's government confirmed plans to legislate that social media platforms must prompt all users to choose between algorithmic and chronological default feeds, with non-compliant platforms facing fines up to $109.2 million.

articles.title: YouTube expands Watch With to more creators
articles.summary: YouTube is widening access to Watch With, a feature first tested in 2024 alongside its NFL livestream coverage, that lets creators record live reactions to other broadcasts. Creators in the expanded experiment group now see a "React live" button in the Share panel on eligible mobile livestreams; tapping it locks their phone camera into horizontal orientation (with no option to disable the camera) and begins broadcasting their reaction. Viewers watching from any device see a combined vertical stream showing both the original content and the reactor's camera feed simultaneously. Creators using the tool can still monetize their reaction streams normally and gain access to shared viewing metrics from the original broadcast. This rollout is part of YouTube's broader push into interactive live content, alongside other tests like gamified livestream leaderboards, 24/7 "livestream stations," and expanded live gifting options. The push comes as YouTube reported in September 2025 that over 30% of daily logged-in users watch live content, underscoring live viewing as a growing engagement and monetization priority for the platform.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is expanding its Watch With feature test, letting more creators broadcast live camera reactions alongside eligible livestreams via a "React live" button, combining both feeds into one vertical stream for viewers.

articles.title: TikTok returns as Toronto International Film Festival platform partner
articles.summary: TikTok has renewed its role as official platform partner of the Toronto International Film Festival for 2026, expanding its involvement to include presenting partner status for this year's Special Presentations program. The deal, which builds on a partnership first launched in 2024, will bring TikTok's biggest group of creators yet to TIFF, with these creators hosting premiere screenings and co-hosting post-screening Q&A sessions alongside filmmakers and cast members. As part of the activation, TikTok is hosting a dedicated event on September 12 featuring actors Caleb Hearon and Zooey Deschanel, who will discuss their upcoming film "Trash Mountain" and talk about how modern audiences discover new stories. TikTok cites internal data showing more than 12 million film and TV posts are published globally on the platform daily, with 35% of users saying TikTok content gives them confidence to try new movies or shows, while separate research found 47% of users have discovered a movie through the app. The continued partnership reinforces TikTok's positioning as a central discovery and promotional platform for entertainment brands and rising creative talent.
articles.li_summary: TikTok is returning as the Toronto International Film Festival's official platform partner for 2026 and presenting partner of the Special Presentations program, bringing its largest-ever creator contingent to host premieres and Q&A sessions.

articles.title: Building a framework to better protect teens on social media
articles.summary: A new review of global teen social media safety efforts highlights growing public support for age restrictions alongside serious enforcement problems. Pew Research's July survey found 56% of Americans back a ban for under-16s, while polls show 90% of UK parents, 79% of French and Italian adults, and 60% of Swedish and Norwegian respondents favor similar limits. Yet Australia, the first country to enact a large-scale under-16 ban, reports in its six-month review that most young users still bypass restrictions, despite testing government ID checks, facial age estimation, and activity-based inference. Regulators found viable verification tools exist but stopped short of mandating one method, leaving enforcement inconsistent. The EU is now trialing government-issued ID for teens, while Meta argues AI and app stores should handle age verification instead. articles.li_summary: Australia's eSafety Commissioner reports that most under-16 users still access banned social platforms six months into its landmark ban, as Pew Research finds 56% of Americans now support similar under-16 restrictions.

articles.title: LinkedIn shares insights into younger professionals
articles.summary: LinkedIn released survey findings from over 18,000 professionals examining how Gen Z employees engage with the workforce and how marketers can better reach this demographic. On the career side, 72% of Gen Z professionals said they miss opportunities due to hesitation, with 37% fearing they'd bother people, 37% fearing judgment, and 34% worried about sounding inauthentic; separately, 53% said they don't know how to start networking professionally. This matters because LinkedIn data shows 27% of Gen Z found their next role through online professional communities, and U.S. applicants with an inside connection were nearly 7 times more likely to get hired. LinkedIn plans to add more in-stream connection features, including expanded in-app games, to help younger users network more easily. On the marketing front, 90% of marketers said future growth hinges on influencing younger decision-makers, 42% said expert-voice content converts best, and 86% of U.S. marketers agreed Gen Z and millennial buyers trust peer recommendations and experts over branded content. Gen Z buyers most engage with short-form and immersive video (49%) and expert content (42%), while 73% of respondents said brand credibility now outweighs visibility.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn's survey of 18,000+ professionals found 72% of Gen Z workers avoid networking out of fear of judgment, while 90% of marketers say growth depends on reaching younger decision-makers via expert-led short-form video.

articles.title: Pinterest offers advice on creating effective shopping promotions
articles.summary: Pinterest released a four-step framework to help brands run more effective shopping promotions ahead of the year-end retail season, tied to its growth to 640 million monthly active users, most of whom use the app for product discovery. The first step, "build foundations," urges brands to set up a shopfront, create product Pins, sync product catalogs for updated listings, and install Pinterest tags for performance tracking before launching ads. Step two, "launch and automate," recommends using Pinterest Trends to spot demand patterns and adopting Performance+, Pinterest's AI tool for automating targeting, bidding, and creative delivery, alongside dynamic retargeting and local inventory ads. The third step focuses on measurement, advising brands to define clear performance benchmarks and monitor campaigns through Pinterest's analytics suite. The final step points marketers to Pinterest Academy, the platform's training program, to deepen understanding of shopping trends and user behavior. Pinterest frames this as a practical, sequential approach for brands looking to strengthen their presence and maximize visibility during peak holiday shopping activity on the platform.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest published a four-step shopping guide for marketers covering profile setup, AI-driven Performance+ ad campaigns, performance tracking, and Pinterest Academy training, as the platform's user base reaches 640 million monthly actives.

articles.title: Zuckerberg is one of the least-liked people in the U.S.
articles.summary: A survey from UMass Lowell's Center for Public Opinion, conducted with YouGov and shared via Reddit's r/DataisBeautiful, ranked Mark Zuckerberg as the least-favorably viewed public figure in America across both major political parties. The finding lands weeks after Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word manifesto describing his vision for AI "superintelligence," where personal AI agents would work around the clock to manage users' health, finances, relationships, careers, and home life. Achieving that vision would require Meta to collect significantly more sensitive personal data than it does today, making public trust a critical factor for adoption. Given Meta's history of privacy controversies, this low favorability rating suggests a steep uphill battle for convincing users to hand over that data. The company's reputation is also being hurt by other issues, including its AI-enabled smart glasses being nicknamed "perve glasses" after reports of wearers secretly filming people. While Meta has recently struck an agreement limiting teen social media use to help rebuild trust, it still faces broad skepticism about whether it operates in the public's interest rather than purely for profit.
articles.li_summary: A new UMass Lowell/YouGov survey found Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is the least-liked public figure in the U.S. among both Republicans and Democrats, complicating his push for AI products that require access to personal data.

articles.title: WhatsApp adds bill payment in India
articles.summary: WhatsApp has introduced a new bill payments feature for users in India, letting them find, track, and pay household and utility bills directly within the app. The tool runs on the Bharat Connect (BBPS) network and connects users to 22,722 billers spanning 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance, credit cards, and loan repayments, while also offering bill summaries and account overviews for easier money management. This builds on existing WhatsApp functions in India such as mobile recharges, transit ticket booking, and government service chatbots, reinforcing Meta's long-running push to turn WhatsApp into an all-purpose "super app" similar to China's WeChat, which is used for shopping, transport, and payments. Progress has been slow due to regulatory hurdles and limited uptake of expanded services in Western markets, but Meta accelerated its India strategy in June by acquiring fintech company Cred and naming its founder, Kunal Shah, as WhatsApp's new head. With 800 million users in India, deeper payment integration could open new revenue streams beyond advertising and strengthen the case for Meta's 2014 WhatsApp acquisition.
articles.li_summary: WhatsApp launched in-app bill payments for its 800 million Indian users, powered by the Bharat Connect (BBPS) network, covering 22,722 billers across 30 categories including electricity, gas, water and insurance.

articles.title: YouTube updates branded content sourcing and disclosures
articles.summary: YouTube announced several updates to its shopping and branded content tools. First, it's piloting an experiment that automatically swaps a creator's tagged affiliate product for the same item sourced from a different eligible local retailer, aiming to test whether faster local delivery boosts sales and commissions; this only applies to Shopping Affiliate program tags, not videos with Paid Product Placement enabled. The test follows YouTube's recent expansion of that affiliate program to include Amazon listings. Separately, YouTube is overhauling branded content disclosure to help creators meet varying international regulations: new, clearer branded content labels will show viewers context instantly, while creators gain settings to restrict sponsored content by age or location, letting them accept brand deals previously blocked by regional legal constraints. YouTube is also introducing automated detection that can apply disclosure labels to newly uploaded videos if its systems spot undisclosed branded content, enforcing compliance without manual creator action. Additionally, the platform updated its paid product placement policy with new terminology aligned to broader industry branded-content standards, giving creators and brands clearer, more consistent rules for sponsorship arrangements.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is testing swapping affiliate product tags for local retailer alternatives to speed delivery, while adding updated branded content labels, age/location restriction controls, and automated disclosure detection for undisclosed sponsored videos.

articles.title: TikTok adds voice and image carousel comments
articles.summary: TikTok has introduced three new comment features aimed at boosting engagement on video posts. Voice comments let users aged 18 and older record audio responses up to 60 seconds long, which appear in the comment section alongside an automatically translated text version; this feature is rolling out globally over the coming month. Comment polls are now available to all creators, letting them add up to five response options directly within the comment section, with results trackable in real time as votes come in—though only the original video creator can create a poll on their post. Photo-based comments are also expanding: users can now attach up to nine images to a single comment, which display as a tappable, scrollable carousel, and live photos can be shared as active-image replies. Standard photo comments are already live worldwide, while the carousel format is being phased in over the next month. Collectively, these tools give viewers more expressive, low-effort ways to react to content beyond typed text.
articles.li_summary: TikTok is rolling out voice comments up to 60 seconds long, creator-only polls with up to five options, and photo carousel replies allowing up to nine images, globally over the next month.

articles.title: Reddit expands AI-powered Max campaigns
articles.summary: Reddit has made its AI-powered Max campaigns available to all advertisers, expanding beyond the select group that tested the automated ad tool since its January launch. Max campaigns automate targeting, creative selection, ad placement, and budget allocation using Reddit's audience insights, which analyze user interests and engagement to improve accuracy. Reddit is also adding three new features: API support so advertisers can build and manage Max campaigns through third-party tools, a new integration with Smartly that lets its users create Max campaigns directly, and "asset groups," which let advertisers organize multiple creative sets—each with its own headlines, media, and destination URLs—within a single campaign, useful for brands managing multiple product lines like running shoes versus training apparel. Reddit reported that during beta testing, advertisers using Max campaigns achieved 17% lower cost-per-acquisition and more than 27% additional conversions on average compared to standard campaigns. The expansion is aimed particularly at brands unfamiliar with Reddit's advertising ecosystem who may have previously hesitated to invest due to a lack of platform expertise.
articles.li_summary: Reddit rolled out its AI-driven Max ad campaigns to all advertisers after January's limited launch, adding API support, a Smartly integration, and asset groups, with beta testers seeing 17% lower CPA and 27% more conversions.
